docs.title: Client integration
docs.html:
Integrating software with FDUpdater

FDUpdater updates an application only after a local administrator registers an exact instance, product and component. Applications keep their own UI and business logic. They implement readiness and health through the public contracts and never add product branches to FDUpdater core.

1. Define stable target identities

Choose lowercase bounded product_id, component_id and per-install instance_id values. A multi-component installation uses one instance and product with separate component IDs. A single-binary product has one component. Keep executable versions separate from configuration, data, credentials, databases, workspaces and logs.

Use fdupdater_conformance::FixtureProduct and validate_matrix to validate the same identity and layout assumptions exercised by the reference products:


use fdupdater_conformance::{FixtureLayout, FixtureProduct, validate_matrix};



let products = vec![

    FixtureProduct::new("suite-a", "product-a", ["server", "agent"], FixtureLayout::MultiComponent)?,

    FixtureProduct::new("suite-b", "product-b", ["desktop"], FixtureLayout::SingleBinary)?,

    FixtureProduct::new("suite-c", "product-c", ["relay"], FixtureLayout::SingleBinary)?,

];

validate_matrix(&products)?;

# Ok::<(), fdupdater_conformance::ConformanceError>(())

2. Register only local authority

Create a TargetReceipt for each component. The receipt supplies the administrator-selected installation root, executable name, service binding, health policy, protected data roots and ownership identities. Release metadata cannot supply or widen any of these values. New targets default to the release channel; an authenticated local operator may set prerelease independently for an exact target.

The installation root and data directories must already exist and must not overlap FDUpdater state or another installation. Use process only for an explicitly supervised child process. Use the matching native service manager for production system services. A systemd or Windows service definition must execute the stable activation path <installation_root>/<executable_name> from its local receipt. FDUpdater atomically materializes the selected hash-verified slot at that path while the service is stopped, then starts the receipt-bound service. Service definitions, arguments and paths remain local administrator policy.

3. Publish the signed release contract

The unified release protocol is shared by the standalone service, embedded clients and FDUpdate Server.

Publish canonical fdupdate/release/v1 data inside fdupdate/signed-release/v1. Each artifact binds the target, platform, architecture, SemVer, HTTPS URL, size, SHA-256, compatibility, rollout, rollback and product-scoped signing key. hawkBit metadata and the standalone manifest provider carry the same signed envelope. Neither transport authorizes a release.

For private standalone delivery, use the runtime gateway provider together with target enrollment. The local target's persisted update_channel is sent on every check, including FDUpdater's own target, and is still enforced locally after the signed response arrives. Approval provides identity only; the server must separately grant the installation access to a repository. Removing either approval or that repository grant prevents new checks, downloads and reports.

Provision public trust keys locally. The runtime never receives a signing private key. A candidate must pass manifest and artifact signatures, replay cursor, channel, platform, architecture, updater-version, installed-version, component dependency, rollout and downgrade checks before staging.

Bootstrap each installation with its own identity

For a standalone target, set enrollment.installation_key_file to a protected file containing the 64-character reusable installation key. Keep the secret out of command arguments and ordinary configuration. code_file remains a mutually exclusive compatibility name for older one-time codes. FDUpdater creates and persists the installation's Ed25519 identity and exact signed request before the first network attempt. An interrupted or offline attempt therefore retries the same identity and consumes no additional server quota; deleting the protected state creates a new identity and consumes a new slot.

The key is attached only while the local enrollment has no authenticated server decision. After the first pending/approved/denied decision, later polling omits the bootstrap key. Update checks, package downloads and reports use only the installation-specific credential from the signed approval decision. A rejected or exhausted key returns the distinct EnrollmentError::Rejected; unavailability remains retryable without replacing the identity.

Embedded applications use fdupdater_enrollment::InstallationKey for their own protected file, stdin, or secret-input path. Its debug representation is always [REDACTED]. Each application instance opens EnrollmentClient with its own state root and instance ID, supplies the key only on the bootstrap request, and then passes the resulting client to fdupdater_app_mode. Reusing one bootstrap key does not share the local private key, instance ID, approval credential, update state or package cache.

Report managed FDUpdater liveness

An approved standalone FDUpdater creates ManagedUpdaterHeartbeat with EnrollmentClient::managed_updater_heartbeat. The client persists and increments the heartbeat sequence before returning the signed document, so a restart or an uncertain network result cannot reuse a sequence. It signs the instance ID, updater version, send time, sequence and random nonce with the same installation Ed25519 identity used for enrollment.

Send the document to POST /v1/updater/{tenant}/{product}/heartbeat with the installation credential as Authorization: Bearer ... and the exact instance ID in X-FDUpdate-Instance. The server requires current approval, matching scope and identity, a valid signature, a bounded timestamp and a sequence greater than the last durably accepted value. A duplicate or older sequence returns 409; invalid credentials, signatures, scopes and revoked identities fail authorization. Liveness is derived from the server receive time. A stale heartbeat is an observation state and never authorizes a release or reports an update failure.

Bind the applications managed by an updater

Approval, heartbeat and repository access do not implicitly give an FDUpdater authority over an application. Using the private operator API, bind the approved updater instance to each exact product/component, repository, platform, architecture and locally selected release channel. Grant check and update separately. Check-only bindings can report installed versions and health but receive no assignment or package.

Binding changes use an expected revision. The first bind uses revision zero; every later bind uses the revision returned by the installation inventory. Unbind disables the policy and advances its revision, so a delayed prior request cannot silently restore authority. The server rechecks the current binding and repository grant during check, package download and result reporting. Revocation, repository removal, channel change or unbind therefore takes effect without rewriting existing assignments.

4. Implement readiness and health

An application that must quiesce implements the authenticated loopback readiness protocol. It stops accepting work, checkpoints active work, flushes durable state, releases exclusive resources and then returns ready. It may return bounded defer_until or reject; timeout and disconnect fail closed.

An Agent supervised by the watchdog implements the authenticated heartbeat protocol. FDUpdater applies a bounded restart budget, exponential backoff and durable quarantine. Diagnostic profiles list exact approved log and crash-metadata paths beneath receipt-owned data roots. Secrets, command arguments and environment-bearing lines must be redacted before persistence or upload.

5. Preserve recovery behavior

Activation stages verified immutable bytes, atomically advances current/previous pointers and performs a bounded health check. Failure restores the previous verified slot. The privileged rollback action uses only a strictly older, hash-verified local previous slot, preserves the replaced current slot, and does not poll or apply a pending provider release. A general downgrade requires a signed authorization bound to the exact installed version. FDUpdater self-update uses the same trust and channel resolver and hands the staged candidate to the independent bootstrap.

6. Run the conformance kit

From a checkout using the supported Rust toolchain:


cargo test -p fdupdater-conformance

cargo test -p fdupdater-conformance --test isolation

The suite proves three unrelated product layouts, mixed versions, simultaneous offers, Linux and Windows contract selection, rollback, server unavailability, per-target channels, readiness decisions, watchdog restart/quarantine, redacted incidents and cross-target isolation. The native activation portion runs on the current host; run it once on each supported operating system before releasing an integration.

docs.title: Self-hosting
docs.html:
Self-host FDUpdate Server

The supported deployment is one Linux host with the FDUpdate TLS edge/services, Eclipse hawkBit 1.1.0, and MariaDB on private container networks. Review server-deployment.md first.

1. Provision a dedicated DNS name and host; expose only TCP 443. 2. Check out and verify an exact FDUpdate release. 3. Keep root-owned config/state outside source and executable trees. Provide TLS, database, operator, signing, OIDC, and storage secrets through protected files. 4. Run server/deploy/fdupdate-server init-config, then validate, install, public-tls, and acceptance with the documented absolute path arguments. 5. Verify TLS health/enrollment and confirm hawkBit, MariaDB, Management API, administration, and diagnostics are not publicly reachable.

Create encrypted consistent database/state backups and an immutable artifact inventory. Restore into isolation and smoke-test enrollment, metadata, download, rollout, feedback, and operators. Test upgrades against a restored backup. When schema rollback is incompatible, restore the whole pre-upgrade recovery point.

See deployment, operations, recovery, and retention.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.html:
FDUpdate

FDUpdate is a secure, product-neutral update platform for Windows and Linux.

  • FDUpdater is a Rust service, CLI, and embeddable contract library. It

    verifies signed releases, stages and atomically activates updates, checks health, and rolls back safely.

  • FDUpdate Server is a self-hosted release, enrollment, rollout, and feedback

    service built around Eclipse hawkBit. Its gateway keeps hawkBit, databases, signing keys, and administration private.

The protocol works with any compatible self-hosted endpoint; the client has no vendor-controlled dependency. update.fedrv.de currently serves the owner's internal installations. A managed public cloud service is not offered today.

Use cases

FDUpdate supports standalone background updates, applications retaining their own installer/UI, public and private repositories, scoped installation grants, staged rollout/rollback, one-time download sharing, server self-update, and COT service Telegram notifications for configured operators.

Quick start

Install the pinned Rust 1.98 toolchain, then:


git clone https://github.com/fedrnv/FDUpdate.git

cd FDUpdate

cargo build --workspace --all-targets --locked

cargo test --workspace --locked

cargo run -p fdupdater --bin FDUpdater -- --version

All supported operations use CLI commands; an IDE is optional. Start with the integration guide, application-managed guide, or self-hosting guide.

Architecture and trust

Remote metadata never grants local paths, services, or keys. Product-scoped Ed25519 signatures, compatibility, replay, rollout and rollback checks run before staging. Activation preserves the prior version with deterministic recovery. Server delivery rechecks installation identity, repository grant, scope and rollout. See architecture and security.

docs.title: Application-managed updates
docs.html:
Application-managed updates

Application-managed mode lets an existing application keep its UI, installer, restart policy and recovery behavior. FDUpdater supplies a versioned Rust check/package/report contract through fdupdater-app-mode; it never receives an application install path and writes packages only below its protected state root.

The application first creates an ApplicationCheckRequest with its installation identity, target, platform, architecture, channel, updater version and installed component versions. ApplicationUpdateService::check accepts remote metadata only through the same approved enrollment gate used by ordinary updates. Its response contains the assignment ID, display version, signed size and digest, release cursor and the exact SignedRelease supplied by the assignment service. The service verifies the release signature, artifact signature, target, compatibility, rollout and release channel before persisting or returning that response.

prepare_package streams the assigned bytes into a bounded temporary file below application-packages, checks the signed size and SHA-256 digest, and atomically caches the verified package. open_package returns a read-only VerifiedPackage stream for the exact assignment after rechecking current enrollment approval and the signed release. The host application copies that stream into its own installer or staging flow. FDUpdater does not modify the application tree, run the installer or restart the application in this mode.

For lightweight self-update without the FDUpdater daemon, implement ApplicationSelfUpdateHost. The library passes only a PackageDescriptor and the already verified VerifiedPackage stream to the host's stage callback. stage_application_update must leave the running installation unchanged and returns an opaque host-owned prepared value. activate_application_update then invokes the host's external restart helper and health check; restart failure, health failure or an unhealthy result invokes rollback_and_restart before an error is returned. rollback_application_update exposes the same exact host rollback for an explicit user action.

The host owns installation paths, atomic replacement and durable recovery for its opaque prepared value. A self-updating process should execute restart and recovery from its installer or a small external helper so interruption cannot leave the running executable half-replaced. The host must preserve the previous verified version until health succeeds. No path, command or helper identity comes from release metadata. A statically linked library is updated only by staging and restarting a newly built owning application; the SDK does not hot-swap library bytes.

After its own installation flow, the application sends an ApplicationReportRequest for the same assignment. An installed result must name the assigned version and requires a previously verified package. failed and deferred results may include a bounded, non-control-character detail for the remote service, while structured audit events contain only the assignment, target, phase, version and outcome. An identical report is idempotent; a conflicting second report is rejected.

Anonymous, pending, denied, revoked and wrong-target identities are rejected before metadata or artifact transport. Approval is checked again for package access and reporting, so later revocation also fails closed. Network retries are explicitly bounded. Invalid signatures, expired or replayed releases, corrupt packages and locally altered assignment metadata are rejected.

Operators can inspect the non-secret local status through the authenticated, read-only loopback API or CLI:


FDUpdater app-updates --endpoint 127.0.0.1:PORT --credential-file ABSOLUTE [--instance INSTANCE_ID]

The result exposes assignment ID, local target, version, phase and final outcome. It excludes enrollment credentials, signed metadata, report detail and package paths.

The server-facing contract fixture and denial matrix run with:


cargo test -p fdupdater-app-mode

cargo test -p fdupdater-app-mode --test denied_states

docs.title: Security
docs.html:
Security and trust model

Networks and distribution are untrusted. Product-scoped Ed25519 keys authenticate canonical releases and artifacts. Sequence, compatibility, platform, rollout, dependency, installed-version and exact rollback rules are checked locally. Size and SHA-256 are verified before staging. Private signing keys never belong to the updater or a long-running server.

Enrollment binds one public key, instance and tenant/product scope. Pending, denied, revoked, wrong-scope, replayed, or ungranted installations receive no metadata or bytes. Operators have individual roles/scopes, short sessions, CSRF protection, and audit. Secrets use protected files/providers, never releases, browser storage, command arguments, or logs. Store failures deny delivery.

The supported Linux deployment separates the public device gateway from the web owner runtime by UID, primary group, secret directory and mutable state. Their only shared filesystem authority is group read access to the Installation Account document and advisory-lock access to one root-provisioned lock file in a directory neither service can modify. The gateway therefore keeps account authority stable through delegated enrollment without gaining write access to account, self-service or administrator state and without access to administrator, COT or web operator credentials.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.html:
Architecture overview

FDUpdater consumes signed product-neutral contracts. Local registration owns paths, service control, health commands, and trusted public keys. The updater verifies, stages, atomically activates, checks health, and preserves rollback.

FDUpdate Server exposes one TLS gateway. FDUpdate services authorize enrollment, repositories, publication, downloads, rollout, feedback, and operator actions. hawkBit 1.1.0 and MariaDB remain private. Signing is a short-lived process with an isolated key. Persistent data, config, secrets, binaries, and logs are separate.

The supported topology is one Linux host and one organization. Tenant-safe extension contracts add default-deny ownership, backend-neutral immutable objects, metering, and quotas without billing, signup, or mandatory cloud service.

Normative decisions: ADR-0001, ADR-0002, ADR-0003, and ADR-0004.

docs.title: Enrollment
docs.html:
Installation enrollment

Each installed application instance has its own Ed25519 identity. FDUpdater generates the key inside its protected local state root, persists it with private-file permissions and sends only a signed enrollment request containing the instance ID, public key and random nonce. Reopening the same instance reuses that identity and the exact pending request; a different instance receives a different key.

The enrollment authority returns a canonical signed decision bound to the request digest, instance and public key. FDUpdater accepts strictly increasing revisions and exposes four states: pending, approved, denied and revoked. A revoked identity cannot return to another state. Approval credentials remain inside the protected signed state and are never returned by status, CLI output or audit records.

Only approved returns a credential, and only for a target explicitly assigned in the decision. Anonymous, pending, denied, revoked and wrong-target requests fail closed before a metadata or artifact transport can be called. Authority unavailability uses a bounded retry count and retains the same signed request.

Installation Account authorization

An installer may authorize the signed software identity with an enabled Installation Account ID or email, its current password, and the exact non-empty set of private repositories requested by the installed software. The request is schema-versioned and sent to the normal product enrollment endpoint. The account must currently grant every requested repository; the server never expands the set from the account's other grants.

The human password exists only in zeroizing request memory and is not written to FDUpdater state, registry state, logs, audit, or the issued installation credential. The account is re-read and authenticated while its durable shared lock is held through the registry decision. Registration quota is counted by distinct signed instance identity; concurrent attempts cannot overrun it.

An identical pending identity is approved with the durable outcome performed_with_installation_account, retaining its earlier submission audit. An exact retry returns the same signed decision without consuming quota. A changed repository set, insufficient grants, wrong password, disabled account, exhausted quota, or revoked identity fails closed. Each successful installation receives its own credential and does not retain the Installation Account password.

Installation keys

An operator can issue a reusable installation key for one product/component with an exact positive registration limit. The server persists only a domain-separated SHA-256 verifier, a non-secret key ID, expiry and disable state, the current repository allowlist, and a ledger of distinct installation instance IDs. The plaintext key is returned only by the issuance response.

Each redemption still carries the installation's own signed Ed25519 enrollment request. A retry of that exact identity is idempotent and does not consume another slot. A different identity consumes one slot, remains pending, and needs normal operator approval. Once the limit is reached, concurrent new identities fail closed. Expiry and disabling stop new identities while preserving idempotent retries and the historical ledger; denial, revocation, or uninstall does not refund a slot.

The operator endpoints are:

  • POST /v1/operator/installation-keys to issue a key with

    max_installations and allowed_repositories;

  • POST /v1/operator/installation-keys/list to return verifier-free key status

    and usage counts;

  • POST /v1/operator/installation-keys/update to change the future admission

    limit/disable state, repository allowlist, or the separate existing-update suspension flag.

The earlier /v1/operator/enrollment-codes issuance route remains compatible and defaults omitted policy fields to a limit of one and an empty repository allowlist. Schema 1 and 2 registry snapshots migrate consumed one-time codes to a one-entry ledger without increasing their access.

Applications can keep their existing UI and read the state through the authenticated local API or CLI:


FDUpdater enrollment --endpoint 127.0.0.1:PORT --credential-file ABSOLUTE [--instance INSTANCE_ID]

The result contains the instance ID, public-key fingerprint, state and decision revision. It contains no private key or approval credential. Enrollment transitions use the structured audit adapter and must be recorded before an approval is committed.

Registration audit

The device gateway atomically persists one redacted event for each distinct registration outcome: pending, denied, approved replay, administrator approval, Installation Account performance, or an unavailable delegated authority. Exact retries are idempotent. Events contain the request digest, outcome provenance, tenant, product, components, complete repository set, optional Installation Account ID, software instance, sequence, and server time. Passwords, installation keys, bearer credentials, signed decisions, email addresses, and request bodies are never stored in this audit.

The authenticated gateway query is POST /v1/operator/registration-audit/query. It accepts bounded time, outcome, product/component, repository, Installation Account ID, instance, and page filters. The caller must supply its complete repository allowlist. An event is visible to a repository-scoped caller only when every repository on the event is within that allowlist; a manipulated repository filter returns no rows. Unscoped events are reserved for the owner view.

The web administration table is /admin/registration-audit. It derives the allowlist from current administrator roles, revalidates every gateway row, uses 25-row pages, and returns Cache-Control: no-store. There is deliberately no CSV or other export route: out-of-scope filters are denied before the gateway is queried, and partial-scope results are never rendered.

The server-facing protocol conformance and denied-state matrix run with:


cargo test -p fdupdater-enrollment

cargo test -p fdupdater-enrollment --test denied_states

cargo test -p fdupdate-device-gateway

docs.title: Operator API
docs.html:
Server operator API and CLI

fdupdate-server-api defines the versioned operator request/response contract used by loopback, mTLS or OIDC transports. Credentials are redacted, stored as hashes and compared without content-dependent early exit. Actors receive explicit roles and tenant/product scopes.

Security administrators register products and approve or revoke installations. Release managers publish immutable releases. Fleet operators start, pause, resume or abort rollouts. Readers access bounded status and diagnostics. A valid role never grants another product scope.

Every request ID is bound to the actor and action. An exact retry returns the original response without a second effect; reuse with another action fails. Authorized, denied and failed first decisions enter a SHA-256 hash-chained audit containing actor, action, scope, result and effect ID, without credentials.

parse_cli_action exposes the matching CLI grammar. The transport reads credentials from protected files and supplies them separately; the CLI grammar deliberately has no credential argument.

Focused verification:


cargo test -p fdupdate-server-api --test conformance --locked

cargo clippy -p fdupdate-server-api --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings

docs.title: Backup and recovery
docs.html:
FDUpdate Server backup, observation and recovery

The recovery archive contains product IDs, approved target IDs, release artifact digests, rollout state and non-secret configuration metadata. It excludes credentials, private keys, secret configuration values and artifact payloads. The archive binds its canonical payload with SHA-256; recovery verifies the complete payload before the operator replaces the last known-good state.

Operational metrics are counters for health failures, rollout pauses, storage use and backup failures. The bounded observation window accepts only compact category/outcome labels and evicts the oldest entry at its configured limit. It does not accept request bodies, credentials or arbitrary log messages.

Credential and signing-key rotation uses distinct key IDs. During the documented overlap deadline, current and previous credentials remain valid; expiry or explicit revocation rejects the old identity. A failed rotation leaves the current identity recoverable. Private signing material remains in the isolated signer and is restored or rotated by its external key-custody procedure, not from a server backup.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.html:
Versioning and compatibility

FDTasks progress uses MAJOR.RELEASE.EPIC.ITEM; release tags identify executable releases. Rust crates have no stable binary ABI, so pin source revisions.

Persisted and exchanged contracts carry exact schema IDs. Unknown versions and fields fail closed. Compatibility changes use a new schema or explicit migration; old state is never guessed. Client/server compatibility follows protocol/schema versions and signed minimum-updater requirements, not matching package versions. Release notes identify migration and rollback impact; validate upgrades against a restored backup. See CHANGELOG.md and self-hosting.

The immutable v1 wire rules, exact platform/ABI matching and release/prerelease selection are defined in the unified release protocol.

docs.title: COT integration
docs.html:
COT service-client integration

FDUpdate Server consumes the current standalone COT service contract rather than embedding COT. The workspace pins COT commit 9f720a6ed5a68dd1fa5df5716fdf7bea57e67c0e, disables default features and enables only cot-sdk/service-client.

The trusted boundary is LocalChannelClient:

  • it accepts loopback HTTP endpoints only;
  • it authenticates with a protected application service credential;
  • channel administration uses cot.private-channels/v1;
  • Telegram setup is write-only and provider secrets remain in COT;
  • list/get/delete use owner-private opaque resources and ETags;
  • delivery uses send_private_message with stable idempotency and correlation

    identities.

Installation Account email self-service additionally uses COT-0473's published cot.private-email-dynamic-recipient/v1 contract: one application-private channel binds the protected sender/provider setup, and each send supplies one validated recipient. FDUpdate uses the typed SDK pinned above and verifies it against a conforming fake COT service. The project owner confirmed the pinned candidate's complete upstream test/conformance result and deployment. The authorized VPS deployment manifest binds the same commit and the running binary digest; its live health probe passes. FDUpdate's focused typed-fixture, security, UI and deployment verification therefore governs compatibility even while the upstream work item remains open for an unrelated lifecycle reason.

NotificationRuntime owns only FDUpdate's bounded routing/handoff file. COT owns its service database, provider adapters, destination data and process lifecycle. Stopping FDUpdate drops the HTTP client; it must not stop the shared COT service.

Updating COT requires an accepted maintenance task, a full immutable source revision, lockfile update and focused adapter/web tests against the new public contract. Read current COT sources and contract documentation from the COT repository; do not copy private implementation details or modify that repository.

Production COT credentials, bot tokens and chat IDs remain outside this repository. Use an isolated loopback fixture for automated verification and a separately authorized environment for any explicitly approved live delivery check.

docs.title: License
docs.html:
FDUpdate license decision

Status: approved by the project owner on 2026-10-18.

The owner selected Apache License 2.0 for FDUpdater, the embeddable libraries, FDUpdate-owned server code, examples and documentation. Apache-2.0 provides an explicit patent grant and termination terms and permits commercial use, including competing hosted services. An OSI-approved license cannot promise to exclude such competition.

Alternatives considered:

  • Apache-2.0 alone keeps the patent terms but removes the simple MIT option.
  • MIT alone is simple but lacks Apache-2.0's express patent language.
  • AGPL-3.0 requires corresponding source for modified network deployments and

    may deter proprietary hosted forks, but adds integration/compliance friction and is not compatible with every intended embedding policy.

The locked Rust dependency graph currently has complete declared license/source metadata and uses permissive expressions (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC, Zlib, Unicode, CC0/CDLA-Permissive and compatible alternatives). COT is MIT OR Apache-2.0. Eclipse hawkBit remains a separate unmodified EPL-2.0 service; its license/notices travel with its image and are not relicensed by FDUpdate.

The repository carries the full terms in root LICENSE, workspace package metadata uses SPDX Apache-2.0, and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md identifies separately licensed dependencies and services. Contributions are offered under Apache-2.0. Repository visibility remains separately controlled by the publication checklist.

Contributing

Discuss material protocol changes first; read AGENTS.md and DEVELOPMENT.md; use the pinned toolchain; run formatting, affected tests, Clippy with warnings denied, and node scripts/check-public-docs.mjs for docs changes. Support

Use GitHub Discussions for questions and Issues for reproducible defects. Include version, OS, component, sanitized logs, expected behavior, and exact CLI steps. Remove secrets, private URLs, customer data, and signing material. Community support is best-effort; no SLA, managed hosting, paid plan, or emergency response is currently offered. Security reports follow SECURITY.md.

FDUpdate release storage architecture — FDFiles protected object interface

Status: owner-directed successor for FDU-EPIC-D010 implementation. The accepted v1 S3 architecture remains immutable historical input.

Boundary

FDUpdate uses the versioned FDFiles v1 integration API as its primary protected store/read boundary. FDUpdate does not receive S3 credentials, bucket names, provider object keys or storage-placement authority. A short-lived service token is supplied by an external secret provider and is sent only to the configured HTTPS control origin.

The implementation is pinned to FDFiles wire version 1 and canonical OpenAPI SHA-256 38dc1b30cbff265d6944f1b37e9168cba64a9155f058a04d131ab85d573e2bf8. That contract belongs to the accepted FDFiles D040 product candidate 932daf9b9d3d1e6075dd6dc490c2b8f0c9557bfd (tree 2d392f1027b0efd5dec89b5333b6e7f673179ade) and was inspected read-only in the FDFiles repository. Its D040 gate and independent review are closed. The public FDFiles origin/main still points to the earlier 9328891 contract and is not deployment-compatible with mirror deletion; production configuration must use an accepted FDFiles build containing D040 or a compatible successor.

The unpublished prototype SDK is not copied or linked: its repository license allows packaging metadata only and forbids distribution without owner approval. FDUpdate implements the bounded HTTP operations required by this architecture.

Service-token issuance follows the normative OpenAPI scopes, not older prose: uploads require resources:write, resource reads and download sessions require resources:read, revision-bound deletion requires resources:delete, and all durable-operation polling requires operations:read. FDUpdate requests these exact scope identities from its external token source and requires separate protected regular token files for least-privilege operation. It does not use the obsolete files:read or files:write names. Different spellings of one path are canonicalized before the CLI accepts them as separate scope files.

Immutable identity

Every stored artifact is identified by its SHA-256, exact byte length, media type and the SHA-256 of the signed release manifest that authorizes it. The portable content key is sha256/<first-two-hex>/<full-digest>. FDFiles resource and revision IDs are opaque locators, never authority or artifact identity.

Publication creates a checksummed upload session, transfers bounded chunks, completes the session and accepts only a returned resource whose size and digest match the immutable identity. Retrieval pins the exact resource revision in a download session, validates range responses and verifies the complete digest before atomic activation by a caller.

Security and failure behavior

  • Control and data clients reject redirects. Authorization is sent only to the

    control origin; data-plane requests receive only the headers returned for the exact capability URL.

  • Production origins require HTTPS. Plain HTTP is allowed only for an explicit

    loopback test configuration.

  • Requests, retries, chunks, responses, operation polling and total artifact

    size are bounded. Uncertain mutations retain stable idempotency keys.

  • Authentication, authorization, version, revision, size and integrity failures

    fail closed and never create a trusted locator.

  • The local backend uses the same identity contract and atomically installs a

    verified content-addressed file without following links.

Revision-bound deletion and remaining distribution boundary

Accepted FDFiles D040 resolves the earlier resource-delete contract gap. DELETE /v1/resources/{resource_id}?revision=... requires a stable Idempotency-Key and a resources:delete token. A stale revision fails without admitting deletion. FDUpdate accepts completion only from the exact durable delete_resource operation, polled with operations:read; retries use a key derived from the journal operation and exact opaque locator. The SDK licensing boundary remains, so no FDFiles package is distributed or linked.

FDU-141 does not delete resources. Its fdupdate-storage publish-stage CLI publishes one verified artifact to primary FDFiles, retrieves it through a read-scoped download session into an immutable VPS content object, then atomically advances a per-product/channel/platform/architecture/variant index. The prior index target remains the known-good fallback. Configuration names separate read_token_file, write_token_file and operations_read_token_file; all must be protected regular files outside the repository. A primary success followed by cache failure is reported as failure and is safe to retry under artifact-derived idempotency keys.

Delayed mirror mutation journal

FDU-143 adds the canonical fdupdate/mirror-mutation-journal/v1 state. Each bounded operation records an immutable ID, create/replace/delete kind, exact primary artifact identity and FDFiles revision, expected mirror revision when applicable, policy version, primary confirmation time and a computed not_before exactly 24 hours later. The journal is atomically persisted behind a separate process lock, rejects symlinks, duplicate IDs, noncanonical state and files larger than 16 MiB, and caps entries at 100,000.

fdupdate-storage mirror-enqueue JOURNAL REQUEST.json records a confirmed primary mutation. Replaying an identical immutable request returns the existing operation; changed input under the same ID conflicts. Enqueueing never contacts or activates a mirror. fdupdate-storage mirror-status JOURNAL REQUEST.json returns either the operation selected by optional operation_id or the bounded complete journal, including durable state, attempts and an explicit failure classification.

fdupdate-storage mirror-execute CONFIG.json REQUEST.json is the only execution entry point. CONFIG.json must explicitly set enabled: true, provide distinct primary and mirror endpoint configurations and non-reused credential files, a real staging directory, the journal path and a separate protected regular authority_public_key_file. The executor never receives the authority private key. With enabled: false, the operation stays pending. Endpoint token files are optional in the common schema but the attempted HTTP operation fails closed unless its exact resources:read, resources:write, resources:delete or operations:read token file is configured.

FDU-180 replaces caller-authored revalidation assertions with fdupdate/mirror-decision/v1. The execution request contains only a canonical base64 payload and Ed25519 signature. The domain-separated payload binds a unique decision and trusted key ID, operation ID and kind, policy version, exact Primary and expected Mirror identities/revisions, authorization and deletion eligibility, retention and last-restorable-backup protection, issue time and expiry. The configured public-key document has schema fdupdate/mirror-authority-key/v1; unknown keys, noncanonical encodings and bad signatures fail before any remote request.

An initial decision must be issued after the full hold, be neither future nor expired and remain within five minutes of execution. Create and replace require the authoritative exact Primary and Mirror state, then download and verify the Primary bytes before a checksummed create or revision-bound replace. Delete requires authoritative Primary absence, explicit eligibility, no retention pin and confirmation that the object is not the last restorable database backup. Changed, unauthorized or protected work is rejected or durably cancelled without remote mutation.

Before remote mutation the journal records running, the decision ID, the digest of the exact signed envelope and not_issued. The FDFiles adapter then classifies the actual resource-mutation boundary as a definitive response or transport / accepted-operation ambiguity; the journal persists definitive_failure, acceptance_unknown or confirmed. A crash before that outcome is durably recorded remains fail-closed as not issued. FDFiles mutation keys make a proven ambiguous retry safe if the process loses the completion response.

An explicit successful FDFiles response whose operation kind, resource shape, locator/revision, size, digest or JSON protocol is invalid is neither confirmed success nor acceptance ambiguity. The adapter and journal persist explicit_invalid_response; even an incorrectly classified Unknown + Identity/Integrity/Protocol result is normalized to that outcome. It remains retryable only with a newly issued fresh exact-operation decision. The expired byte-identical exception additionally requires acceptance_unknown with an unavailable transport/observation failure, so an invalid explicit response cannot manufacture authority merely by being retried.

An expired byte-identical decision may be reused only for the same operation whose persisted outcome is acceptance_unknown. Primary retrieval failures, local preparation failures, definitive 4xx/conflict responses and legacy records without the outcome cannot spend expired authority; they require a new, fresh, independently signed exact-operation decision. Changed payloads and cross-operation replay remain rejected. A bounded remote failure records retryable_failure and increments the attempt count; success records the exact returned mirror locator, or no locator for deletion. Temporary verified primary copies are removed when the command exits. No production mirror, credentials or provider placement are created by this implementation.

Verified download fallback

FDU-142 adds an optional tiered download runtime to fdupdate-web. The release catalog remains the authorization authority: public and authenticated routes must authorize the exact project, release and SHA-256 before any storage lookup or network request. A separate bounded tier catalog maps that exact tuple to an immutable primary locator, an optional explicitly configured mirror locator and the product/channel/platform/architecture/variant VPS cache key.

The resolver tries primary FDFiles, then the configured mirror, then an exact current or previous known-good VPS cache entry. Every tier must reproduce the catalogued size and SHA-256 before the file is exposed. Failed and corrupt candidates are removed. The mirror is disabled when it is absent from both the catalog record and runtime configuration; this feature does not activate a production mirror.

VPS fallback is copied to an isolated spool file and served through the normal range-capable gateway. Its body owns a non-blocking concurrency permit until the response is dropped, enforces a configured byte rate, and participates in a sliding one-minute request limit. Spool files are removed on completion, disconnect and invalid range. Older releases are served from VPS only when the requested immutable identity is the exact current or previous retained entry; otherwise the gateway returns service unavailable without substituting a newer release.

The tiered runtime accepts only protected resources:read token files and bounded FDFiles clients. Production control origins remain HTTPS-only. Operators must configure catalog_file, vps_cache_root, spool_root, primary read settings and all three VPS limits; an optional mirror uses the same read-only contract. Startup rejects unsafe paths, zero limits and invalid catalogs.

Encrypted FDUpdate state backup and staging restore

FDU-144 adds the canonical fdupdate/encrypted-backup/v1 envelope and fdupdate/backup-catalog/v1 recovery catalog to fdupdate-storage. The backup input is a database-native or quiesced snapshot set, not arbitrary live files. Every request carries one stable generation marker and must contain database, release catalog and installation-registry roles; a WAL may be included. The marker is read before and after copying, every source must remain the same regular non-symlink file while copied, and every copied byte receives a SHA-256 entry in the authenticated snapshot manifest. The producer must advance the marker for each state transaction or create the inputs while the service is quiesced. The backup command fails closed if that consistency contract is not met.

The snapshot is encrypted in bounded 1 MiB chunks with XChaCha20-Poly1305. A random 128-bit nonce prefix plus a monotonic 64-bit chunk index gives every chunk a distinct nonce; the complete public envelope header and chunk index are additional authenticated data. The encrypted object identity covers its exact bytes, while signed_manifest_sha256 in the shared storage identity carries the authenticated snapshot-manifest digest for this non-release object. Backup key files contain exactly 32 bytes encoded as 64 hexadecimal characters, remain outside the catalog and envelope, cannot be reused as any FDFiles scoped token or snapshot input, and must be protected by the host ACL. Key loss is intentionally not bypassed: restore fails rather than weakening confidentiality.

fdupdate-storage backup-create CONFIG.json REQUEST.json creates or safely reuses an immutable local encrypted archive, verifies a complete decrypt in a disposable directory, writes it to Primary FDFiles with resources:write and operations:read, then records a mirror-create operation through the FDU-143 journal. The journal confirmation time is the successful Primary operation, so the mirror cannot execute before the mandatory 24-hour hold. Primary and mirror service credentials remain scope-specific. The bounded local recovery window retains at least two newest verified encrypted archives; pruning never deletes a Primary object or the catalog record, and interrupted pruning can only leave an extra local copy.

fdupdate-storage backup-restore CONFIG.json REQUEST.json downloads the exact recorded Primary resource with resources:read, verifies its encrypted object identity, authenticates and decrypts every chunk into a disposable directory, then verifies the manifest, role set, sizes and SHA-256 of every restored file. Only the fully verified directory is atomically renamed to a new RESTORE_ROOT/BACKUP_ID staging path. An existing destination is never replaced; activation or live database replacement remains a separate owner-controlled operation. backup-status CATALOG.json REQUEST.json exposes immutable Primary, mirror-queue, local-copy and last successful restore evidence for FDU-145.

The initial implementation accepts at most 128 inputs and 512 MiB of snapshot payload. It deliberately performs no live migration, key escrow, production provider provisioning, automatic Primary deletion or mirror activation. A 24-hour-delayed mirror can lag by at least a day and is not advertised as zero-loss recovery; database-native snapshots/WAL and the local recovery window remain required.

Replica, retention and restore health

FDU-145 adds a bounded offline scrub command and an owner-only rendering of its validated result. fdupdate-storage health-scan CONFIG.json REQUEST.json accepts an empty request and a configuration containing report_file, tier_catalog_file, vps_cache_root, mirror_journal_file, backup_catalog_file, staging_root, primary, optional mirror, thresholds and rates. The Primary and optional Mirror endpoints must be distinct and use distinct credential files. Scrubbing only reads remote objects, so each configured endpoint needs only the normative FDFiles resources:read service token; no documentation-only files:* scope is accepted. The local journal, rather than remote operations polling, remains the replication-state authority.

For every retained release and encrypted backup, the scrub downloads the exact immutable locator into a disposable staging directory and verifies size and SHA-256 through the normal storage client. It separately verifies current and previous VPS cache bytes, local encrypted backup archives, delayed mirror journal state and recorded restore timestamps. The resulting fdupdate/storage-health-report/v1 records explicit healthy, disabled, queued, running, retrying, failed, missing, not-retained, unauthorized, unavailable, corrupt and protocol-error states. It also records queue age and overdue counts, backup/restore age alerts, unique retained bytes, VPS free bytes, configured capacity thresholds and operator-supplied USD-micro/GiB storage and scrub-egress estimates. Rates are estimates, not provider billing data.

The report is atomically replaced, rejects symlinks, is bounded to 32 MiB and contains no bearer token, encryption key or plaintext backup content. fdupdate-storage health-status REPORT.json REQUEST.json validates and prints it. fdupdate-web may set storage_health_report_file; startup rejects an invalid initial report and /admin/storage-health reloads it on every request. Only an owner session can access the page. A report older than its embedded freshness threshold is prominently marked stale and makes no current-health claim; a missing or corrupt replacement returns service unavailable without partial totals.

The scrub includes a dry cleanup plan for files below the VPS cache's objects/sha256 directory that are not referenced as current or previous. fdupdate-storage cache-cleanup CONFIG.json REQUEST.json is the only cleanup entry point. Its request must repeat the exact cache-state SHA-256 and cleanup fingerprint from a fresh report, set explicit nonzero maximum file and byte bounds, and set apply to opt into deletion. Publication and cleanup share a cross-process mutation lock and reload the durable index while locked, so a publication after preview invalidates the request before any deletion. Cleanup also re-verifies every retained object before applying the plan. It cannot address Primary, Mirror, backups, catalog records or remote APIs, and it cannot bypass the FDU-143 24-hour mirror hold. Corrupt retained cache state therefore blocks cleanup instead of risking loss.

docs.title: FDUpdate release storage architecture — primary S3, future mirror, VPS latest-copy cache
docs.description: FDUpdate FDUpdate release storage architecture — primary S3, future mirror, VPS latest-copy cache documentation.
docs.html:
FDUpdate release storage architecture — primary S3, future mirror, VPS latest-copy cache

Status: owner-approved target architecture; implementation and live migration not started.

Storage tiers

1. Primary: Hetzner Object Storage S3 or compatible alternative; immutable content-addressed artifacts and signed manifests for every retained release and prerelease. 2. Secondary: independent S3 mirror (prefer distinct provider/region and failure domain), planned but not deployed now; eventually replicate all retained versions, with verified object checksums and delayed/versioned deletion protection. 3. Local VPS: verified latest stable release and latest prerelease per product, channel, OS, architecture and required package variant, not just one global file. VPS copies are both recovery cache and last-known-good fallback; reserve sufficient disk and capacity alerts.

Publication and activation

  • CI manual publish uploads to Primary, validates digest/size/signature and commits immutable catalog metadata.
  • Stage the new latest package to VPS and verify it before evicting prior local copy; maintain at least one previously known-good candidate during replacement.
  • Define clear readiness semantics: publishing a release may be blocked or marked degraded if latest VPS copy is not safely present; never claim three replicas before mirror activation.
  • When mirror is enabled, asynchronous replication has tracked pending/verified/failed states and alerts. Never infer successful mirror write from a queued job.
  • Manifest/catalog metadata, encryption/signing keys, installation registry and DB require separate backup and restore, not merely artifact copies.

Download and failure

  • Primary direct download with short-lived authorized URL for private artifacts; fallback to independently verified Mirror when enabled.
  • If both S3 locations unavailable, latest local VPS copy can be served through authenticated FDUpdate gateway with strict bandwidth/concurrency/rate limits.
  • Older versions are unavailable during primary outage until mirror is enabled; avoid claiming always-on service: VPS/network/API are shared failure domains.
  • Every fallback verifies exact immutable artifact digest and signed manifest; no downgrade or private-to-public disclosure.
  • Health checks, reconciliation, periodic scrub, orphan cleanup, corruption quarantine and restore drills.

Retention and deletion

  • Configurable stable/prerelease retention per repository (default 10 each from existing requirements).
  • Pin latest local variants and all objects required by active rollout/rollback; stage replacements atomically.
  • Mirror deletion must not blindly propagate accidental primary deletion; use object versioning or protected deletion grace and restore process.
  • Account for VPS local disk, primary/mirror storage, egress, request charges and API proxy costs.

Proposed FDTasks successor scope

  • Storage provider abstraction and S3 backend.
  • Atomic primary publication and local latest-copy cache.
  • Fallback download selection, integrity and access control.
  • Mirroring interface and replication journal (future mirror inactive).
  • Scrub, retention, metadata backups, restore and failure tests.
  • Admin dashboard showing replica health, cache occupancy, per-release copies, alerts and costs.
  • One targeted gate and independent review under a next development Epic; avoid modifying accepted D009 task specs and follow FDTasks 5.5 append-only rules.

No production DNS, S3 credentials, live releases or billing changed by this document.

Owner-approved 24-hour delayed mirror and database backup policy (2026-10-18)

  • VPS holds the live database. Create consistent, encrypted, restorable database backups in Primary S3, including required catalog, enrollment and installation metadata; replicate backups to Mirror S3.
  • Every mirror mutation (create, overwrite where permitted, and delete) executes no earlier than 24 hours after the corresponding primary operation has been durably confirmed and validated. Queue an immutable operation record with source object version/digest, primary confirmation timestamp and mirror-not-before timestamp.
  • At execution time revalidate source object version, cryptographic digest, authorization, retention pins and current deletion eligibility. Stale or superseded operations must be cancelled/reconciled, not blindly replayed.
  • Mirror deletes require verified primary deletion eligibility and independent second check after the full delay; do not delete the last known restorable database backup or protected release.
  • The delay applies to new backups as well: mirror recovery point may be at least 24 hours behind primary. Protect this window with Primary S3 object versioning/immutability and local database WAL/snapshot retention; do not advertise zero data loss.
  • A 24-hour delayed mirror is a replication target, not a complete backup defense against ransomware or credential compromise. Use separate credentials, versioning/Object Lock where supported, restore drills and tested offsite recovery.
  • Monitor replication queue age, lag, failed verification, backup age, restore success and retained storage size. Make the delay configurable only through a future explicit policy change; initial mandatory minimum is 24 hours.
  • No live mirror is provisioned in this phase; preserve interfaces and migration plan.

docs.title: SaaS-ready foundations
docs.html:
SaaS-ready foundations

FDUpdate remains a self-hosted, single-organization product. The fdupdate-saas-foundation crate defines extension contracts needed by a future managed service without adding signup, billing, pricing, or cloud dependencies.

Every application, repository, release, installation key, installation, feedback record, artifact, and audit event has one validated organization owner. Existing server tenant plus repository/product scope is the current ownership source. Authorization compares trusted session/credential scope with stored ownership; client-supplied tenant text never grants access. Colliding IDs across organizations remain distinct and failures deny access.

StorageBackend binds immutable SHA-256/length identities to organization-owned objects. The local backend stays the default. An S3-compatible implementation must pass the same identity, immutability, ownership, corruption, and unavailable-store contract before selection; bucket/object URLs never become authorization.

UsageLedger accepts organization-scoped idempotent event IDs and counts stored bytes, egress bytes, and registered installations. Quota can deny a proposed delta before effect. These are policy hooks, not billing records; they contain no price, payment, invoice, customer secret, or mandatory remote call.

Legacy state migrates only with an administrator-selected default organization. The migration writes explicit owners, validates the result, and retains the pre-migration backup for rollback. It never infers multiple organizations from product names, repositories, hostnames, or credentials.

docs.title: Client feedback
docs.html:
Client feedback

Integrated applications use fdupdate-feedback to create feedback or bug reports and keep a bounded durable retry queue. The application supplies its own current target and installed version from the same local receipt/registry it uses for update checks. It never accepts an installation ID, tenant or repository from the user. The gateway derives those values from the authenticated installation credential and its last reported application state.


use fdupdate_feedback::{FeedbackKind, FeedbackQueue, FeedbackRequest};



# fn example(state_root: &std::path::Path, target: fdupdate_contract::Target,

#            installed: fdupdate_contract::Version) -> fdupdate_feedback::Result<()> {

let request = FeedbackRequest::new(

    "ui-20261018-0001",

    target,

    FeedbackKind::Bug,

    "Window does not open",

    "Opening the main window leaves the process in the background.",

    1_792_300_000,

    installed,

    None, // diagnostics require an explicit Some(...)

)?;

FeedbackQueue::open(state_root)?.enqueue(request)?;

# Ok(()) }

A transport submits the oldest queued request as JSON to POST /v1/feedback/{tenant}/{product} with the installation credential as Bearer authorization and X-FDUpdate-Instance. submit_next removes a request only after the transport accepts it and the shorter queue is durably committed. A transient outage leaves the original request ID and submitted version intact for an idempotent retry.

The request is limited to a 160-byte subject, 8 KiB body, three explicitly opted-in text diagnostics, 16 KiB per diagnostic and 32 KiB total diagnostic text. Diagnostic labels are basename-only. Both the client constructor and server store redact complete lines containing authorization, password, secret, token or credential markers. The adapter never reads host files automatically.

The server authenticates the installation and component, requires prior reported installed state, and records the client-reported version beside the server's last-known installed version. It labels them match, mismatch or unknown and never substitutes an assigned or available release. Tenant, installation, repository, platform, architecture and channel are server-derived. A changed reuse of a request ID conflicts; an exact retry returns accepted: false. New reports are limited to 20 per installation per hour and the durable store is bounded to 100,000 records.

The client request ID is idempotency provenance within one installation. On first acceptance the server derives a separate stable report ID from the tenant, product, installation and client request ID. Operator URLs, workflow mutations, duplicate links and audit use that server report ID, so two installations may safely choose the same client request ID. Current gateway and feedback snapshots require their feedback section and every workflow field. Explicit schema-1 migration derives the same stable IDs and rejects ambiguous legacy duplicate links; malformed current snapshots fail before state becomes visible.

HTTP responses use 401 for invalid/revoked identity, 409 for missing installed state or changed duplicate, 429 for the per-installation rate limit, 507 for exhausted durable capacity and 503 when the atomic gateway snapshot cannot be committed.

Administrator inbox

Owners, fleet operators and security administrators open /admin/feedback. The server requests only products represented by repositories visible to the account and filters each report again by its server-derived repository. The inbox supports bounded search, status/type filters and 25-record pages. Report details link to the exact installation and repository and keep the original reported version beside the current server-last-known version.

Workflow changes use the stable server report ID, the report's current revision and the administrator session CSRF token. New, In progress, Resolved and Closed status, internal notes and same-repository duplicate links persist in the gateway snapshot. A stale revision returns conflict. Original subject, body, version, identity, timestamps and diagnostics never change; every workflow mutation appends actor/time/status/note metadata to a bounded audit trail. Restoration reconciles each note with exactly one audit revision, enforces ordered server timestamps and rejects self-links or duplicate cycles. All client text, diagnostic names/content and note text are HTML-escaped. The page uses Cache-Control: no-store and switches filters and workflow controls to one column below 600 px.

docs.title: COT service notifications
docs.html:
COT service notifications

FDUpdate Server uses cot-sdk at immutable COT revision dd7496c14bf3526fd93d8b92c00ede34f8ae3c05 with default features disabled and only service-client enabled. FDUpdate does not embed a COT provider, open a COT database, or own the COT process lifecycle.

Enable notifications by setting all three values in the protected fdupdate-web JSON configuration:


{

  "notification_state_dir": "/var/lib/fdupdate/notifications",

  "cot_service_endpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:8081/",

  "cot_service_credential_file": "/etc/fdupdate/cot-service.credential"

}

The endpoint must be loopback. The credential file must be a regular, non-symlink file no larger than 512 bytes and readable only by the FDUpdate service account. COT must authorize that credential as the FDUpdate application. Production credentials, provider secrets and destination identifiers stay outside this repository.

Owners create Telegram channels from /admin/notifications. FDUpdate passes the write-only bot token and chat ID into COT private-channel protected setup; COT owns the secret, destination, channel lifecycle and provider deduplication. FDUpdate stores and displays only COT's opaque channel ID, safe display label, lifecycle state, revision and ETag. It can list, test and conditionally delete its own private channels. Stale ETags fail closed.

FDUpdate persists a bounded event-to-COT handoff before calling send_private_message. A logical message ID binds the event, route, opaque channel ID and channel ETag, so equal ETags on different COT channels cannot collide. The event ID is also passed as correlation ID. Each attempt rechecks that the channel is still ready with the exact bound identity and revision. Changed or removed authority cancels unsent work rather than retargeting it.

States are queued, retrying, in_flight, sent, uncertain, failed, expired and cancelled. sent means COT reported provider acceptance or an already-processed idempotent message; it is not proof that a person read it. Timeout or transport loss after a send is uncertain because the provider may already have accepted the message. Operator retry retains the same logical identity and can still duplicate at a provider that cannot guarantee idempotency.

The handoff remains limited to 4096 jobs, 64 jobs per pass, five admitted attempts, 4096 message bytes and 24 hours lifetime. Feedback and update transactions never depend on COT availability. Rules remain disabled on first creation, previews do not send, repository-scoped administrators see only authorized rule/history projections, and all browser mutations require a valid session and CSRF value.

Legacy v1/v2 embedded-COT handoff files upgrade to v3. Nonterminal legacy jobs are cancelled with cot_service_migration_required; provider credentials and destinations are deliberately not imported from the old embedded state.
